chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammara, from his father. He said: I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him):

I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about God — does He have pleasure and displeasure? He said: Yes, but not in the way that is found among creatures. Rather, the anger of God is His punishment, and His pleasure is His reward.

key_terms.ثَوَابُهُ: Thawabuhu (His reward): The reality of what is referred to as God's pleasure
key_terms.رِضًا: Rida (pleasure/contentment): When attributed to God, it signifies His reward and grace, not an emotional state
key_terms.سُخْطٌ: Sukht (displeasure/anger): When attributed to God, it signifies His punishment, not a human-like emotion
key_terms.عِقَابُهُ: 'Iqabuhu (His punishment): The reality of what is referred to as God's anger

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about God's pleasure and anger?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Muhammad ibn 'Ammara asks Imam al-Sadiq about whether God experiences pleasure and anger. The Imam confirms that God does indeed have pleasure (rida) and displeasure (sukht), but clarifies that these attributes are fundamentally different from the emotions found in creatures. God's anger is to be understood as His punishment, and His pleasure as His reward. This teaching reflects the Shia theological principle of tanzih (divine transcendence), affirming God's attributes while denying any anthropomorphic interpretation.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Sikri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ammara from his father. He said: I asked al-Sadiq Ja

`far b. Muhammad (as), saying to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me regarding Allah: does He become pleased and discontented? So, he said: Yes, but not in the way that is present among the creatures. Rather, the anger of Allah is His punishment, and His pleasure is His reward.
